findings.note: Lost/corrupted audit row: record.appendRow opens .metareview/runs.jsonl with os.O_CREATE|os.O_RDWR (no O_APPEND) and writes with Seek(0,2) followed by Write, relying on an advisory flock. Every other writer of the same file (internal/state.AppendJSONL, used by artifactreview, epicready, taskdone and prready) opens with O_APPEND and takes no lock, so the lock provides no mutual exclusion against them. If one of those processes appends between record's Seek and its Write, record writes at the now-stale offset and overwrites that row's bytes instead of appending after it — a silently corrupted line and a lost run record, in the file the gates read back for run-chain resolution. Opening with O_APPEND for the write (reopening for the truncate repair) makes the append atomic and matches the file's established contract.

evidence.note: os.OpenFile(p, os.O_CREATE|os.O_RDWR, 0o644) — O_APPEND is absent.
steps append Seek(0, 2) then Write: the offset is resolved before the write, not atomically with it.
The pre-existing runs.jsonl writer uses os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY|os.O_APPEND and never calls flock, so it does not cooperate with record's advisory lock.

findings.note: Same non-cooperative-lock premise on the torn-tail repair: appendRow classifies the bytes after the last newline as a torn fragment from a snapshot read, then f.Truncate(t.offset) removes them. A complete row appended by a non-locking writer in that window is removed from runs.jsonl. It is quarantined under .metareview/runs/.torn rather than destroyed, so this is recoverable, but the row disappears from the log the gates read.

findings.note: Documentation states an invalidation rule the planner does not guarantee. All three docs in this shard say editing a file invalidates only its own shard's result and the rest can be left alone, unconditionally. PlanShards derives the bucket depth from total branch bytes (bits = bucketBits(needBuckets(total, budget))), so an edit that pushes the diff across a bucket-bits boundary re-buckets every path and changes every shard id and hash — the repository's own TestBitsBoundaryRecutsAll asserts exactly that. The failure mode is safe (unmatched results are ignored and the gate reports the uncovered shards), but a driver following the docs will burn a round. The docs need the boundary caveat, or the guidance should be to re-read plan.json after each fix round.

evidence.note: bits depends on total bytes, so shard identity is not stable across a bucket-count change.
TestBitsBoundaryRecutsAll: "crossing the bits boundary must re-cut the plan".
"Editing a file invalidates only its own shard's result ... leave the rest" — stated without the boundary caveat; commands/review-task-done.md:32 repeats it.

findings.note: record.Terminal checks ctx.Err() once and then calls appendRow, which takes a blocking syscall.Flock(LOCK_EX) with no deadline and no context awareness: a stale holder hangs the CLI with no diagnostic. The project's other flock user takes LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB and surfaces a typed CodeRunLocked error instead.

evidence.note: flock(int(f.Fd()), syscall.LOCK_EX) — blocking, after the only ctx check.
syscall.Flock(int(f.Fd()), syscall.LOCK_EX|syscall.LOCK_NB) with an EWOULDBLOCK to CodeRunLocked mapping.
